qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Scale economies shared in Medicare Advantage membership and CenterWell senior clinics provide operational efficiency, but fail to produce economic moats. 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 11.2% falls short of the 12% hurdle. Pricing power is structurally absent as rates are dictated by CMS benchmark calculations, statutory 85% MLR floors, and Star Ratings bonus metrics rather than commercial market power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC 11.2% < 12%, REJECT). As a concentrated Medicare Advantage insurer, Humana is a price-taker bound by CMS reimbursement rate updates, Star Ratings quality bonuses, and statutory medical loss ratio caps. Unable to independently raise prices to match medical cost inflation, resulting in sub-hurdle multi-cycle ROIC.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 11.2%, failing the 12% minimum hurdle. Recent annual ROIC has compressed further to 7.8% (2023), 9.0% (2024), and 8.1% (2025). The business is heavily concentrated (>80% of revenue) in Medicare Advantage, exposing it to unilateral CMS rate decisions and star rating recalculations. The drop in 4+ star member coverage from 94% to ~25% in 2025 triggered a $3.0B-$3.5B high-margin bonus revenue headwind, while medical benefit ratios surged to 90-95% due to elevated post-pandemic utilization without price-offset mechanisms.
